newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia flood toll at 14 as U.S. pledges aid.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia flood toll at 14 as U.S. pledges aid.

text.p: The death toll from flooding on the Mekong River in Cambodia rose to 14 on Tuesday as aid began to trickle in for the hundreds of thousands left homeless.
The latest reports showed 14 people had died in the floods, including one in Phnom Penh, said Uy Samath, Red Cross' Disaster Management Department director, on Tuesday.

Uy Samath said an estimated 1.3 million people were homeless and 450,000 faced food shortages. Cambodia has a population of about 10.5 million. About quarter of a million hectares of rice fields had been flooded, he said.
The U.S. embassy said it would donate $25,000 to help the victims.

"I have determined that a disaster has occurred and have committed the full amount of funds available to me," U.S. ambassador Kenneth Quinn told reporters, adding that the aid would be forwarded to the Cambodian Red Cross for emergency goods such as food, water and tarps.
Quinn said he had asked for a special assessment team to travel to Cambodia "to determine whether additional assistance could usefully be provided".

Co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen earlier this week called on the local and international communities to help victims of the flooding, which has hit provinces stretching from Laos to Vietnam. Hun Sen said about $70,000 had been received so far.
